title: JNIM-FLA Assault Overruns Malian Army Position at Dioura — 100+ Soldiers Killed, 100+ Taken Hostage
detail: Fighters from the al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimin (JNIM), reportedly acting alongside the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), overran a Malian army position at Dioura, Ténenkou Cercle, Mopti Region, on September 10, 2026. Casualty figures diverge sharply between sources: an unnamed security source told Reuters 130 soldiers were killed and more than 100 taken hostage; an unnamed diplomatic source put the toll at roughly 120 killed; JNIM's own claim, issued the following week, was 150 soldiers killed. Mali's military did not release an official toll, saying only that it launched a retaliatory operation lasting more than a week and inflicted "significant losses" on the attackers. Reuters reported the competing figures on September 21, citing the sensitivity of the matter for its sources' anonymity. If confirmed, the toll would rank among the deadliest single losses for Mali's army since the war began, compounding pressure from JNIM's ongoing blockade of Bamako.
